notes: Object insert through created (inverse created_by). The edit's 'signed on its base' is part of the inserted fact (SignedWork). q3 ('is the Pietà the only work he signed?') is determinate 'no' since 2026-10-31 (FINDINGS A1): the Wrenhallow Madonna is a second signed work, distinct from the Pietà, so the closed claim is inconsistent with the KB. The worlds differ only on the count (q2, fol, arithmetic), so they carry no axioms; w1 is no longer an exception. The ceiling bridge uses a relation. 2026-10-31 (justify.py): q3's 'no' is built from the edit and new_work ('A relief first found in a Tuscan chapel in 2025 is a different work from the Pietà in St. Peter's Basilica.', its bridge, a firm fact: the new item is newly found, so not the known one); 'Michelangelo's Pietà in St. Peter's Basilica is the only work he ever signed.' is q3's revision fact (the uniqueness belief that gives way; the answer never uses it).

bridge_refs.new_work: A relief first found in a Tuscan chapel in 2025 is a different work from the Pietà in St. Peter's Basilica.

revision_refs.pieta: Michelangelo's Pietà in St. Peter's Basilica is the only work he ever signed.

queries.not_checked: fol (arithmetic): counts the members of a collection

fol.notes: Works are an uninterpreted sort; created and signed are beliefs (uninterpreted). w1 stores the count as a figure (number_of_members, ATTRIBUTES.md), which the insert does not recompute; w2 stores the counting rule over the stored list (an entry counts only if it differs from the earlier ones, so the new member's distinctness enters the count). Counting needs a closed world: every member the model knows is one of the named constants (presupposition named_only; Z3 does not need it to fix the value). The new member's distinctness from the stored one is part of the edit ('newly found').

pieta_signed.says: Michelangelo's signed works: the Pietà. (stored, as a list)

named_only.says: Every signed work by Michelangelo the model knows of is one of the named ones. (closed world)
named_only.z3: ForAll(x, Implies(And(created(michelangelo, x), signed(x)), Or(x == pieta, x == wrenhallow)))

stores: number_of_members(michelangelo_signed_works) == count(And(created(michelangelo, pieta), signed(pieta)), And(And(created(michelangelo, wrenhallow), signed(wrenhallow)), pieta != wrenhallow))
